clue.text: Staffs man employed in counting sheep, originally

indicators.note: employed in says one piece is set to work inside the letters of another
originally points to the opening letters of counting and sheep

parts.note: a rook is a chessman, so man can mean a chess piece

explanation.surface: A Staffordshire fellow is hired to count sheep at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staffs' looks like the abbreviation for Staffordshire, an English county, but it is the plural of staff: shepherds' sticks. 'employed in' puts ROOK inside C and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A shepherd's crook is a hooked staff, so staffs of that kind are crooks.

clue.text: Cheese's left out for after start of chess game

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of chess
left out says the letters of for are removed from the cheese

parts.note: Roquefort is a French blue cheese
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cheese is set aside for after the opening of a chess match.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': the cheese is left out for, i.e. loses those three letters. 'Chess game' looks like the definition, but chess only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Croquet is a lawn game of knocking balls through hoops with mallets.

clue.text: Auxiliary indicating one should 12 4 across, centrally

indicators.note: centrally says the letters come from the middle of the linked answer at 12 and 4 across

explanation.surface: A helping verb saying one must pass through, in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits at the centre of the sixteen-letter answer to 12 and 4 across, spanning the end of its second word and start of its third.
explanation.definitionFit: A modal auxiliary verb expressing obligation, as in you should go.

clue.text: Animal found swimming in a lake or a bay, primarily

indicators.note: swimming says the letters are moving about and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letter of bay

explanation.surface: A creature is spotted swimming in a lake or bay.
explanation.walkthrough: A, LAKE, OR, A and B (first of bay) are rearranged together. Koalas do not swim much, which adds to the deception.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala is an Australian marsupial, an animal often loosely called a bear.

clue.text: See 12
Roman sporting catsuit

indicators.note: sporting, as in playing about, signals that the letters of catsuit are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Roman wearing a figure-hugging catsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' reads as wearing, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a Roman historian and senator of the first century AD.

clue.text: Become member of board

definitions.meaning: to join an organisation, as in to enrol in a profession
to get on a ship, plane or train

explanation.definitionFit: Entering a body means joining it; entering a vehicle means getting aboard it.

clue.text: Hiding given by wielding short scourge in first of beatings

indicators.note: wielding, as in brandishing, signals the letters are shaken into a new order
short says the word scourge loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of beatings

explanation.surface: Someone is concealed while a whip is brandished at the start of a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOURG (scourge cut short), IN and B are rearranged under 'wielding'; 'given by' links. Hiding looks like a beating, but means concealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscuring something conceals it from view, which is hiding it.

clue.text: Yacht with power supply that's irregular

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: supply read as an adverb, supplely, signals the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A yacht with its own power source that is erratic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun, as in power supply, but is an adverb meaning flexibly, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something patchy is uneven in quality or spread, so irregular.

clue.text: Mark fools about to a degree

indicators.note: about says the word for fools is turned round

parts.note: gits is British slang for stupid people
an MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: Note that idiots dither to some extent.
explanation.walkthrough: GITS turned by 'about' gives STIG, followed by MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace, a stain on someone's reputation.

clue.text: Bacchanalian celebration beginning after giro blown on wine

indicators.note: after says the first letter of celebration comes at the end, following the rest
blown, as in blown apart, signals that the letters of giro are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

indicators.note: beginning picks the opening letter of celebration

explanation.surface: A celebration starts once a welfare cheque has been splurged on wine.
explanation.walkthrough: A giro was a British welfare cheque. 'on' just places the wine after the anagram in an across clue, and 'after' sends the first letter of celebration to the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchanalian revels are drunken and wild, which is exactly what an orgy-like, orgiastic party is.

clue.text: Film on cross-dressers seen here?

indicators.note: on in an across clue says the film's letters follow those for the cross-dressers

parts.note: TVs is short for transvestites
E.T. is Spielberg's film about an extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: Where might one watch a movie about cross-dressers?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a film about cross-dressers would be watched on a television.
explanation.definitionFit: A television receiver is where broadcast films of any kind are watched at home.

clue.text: Extremely uneven unlit B-road

indicators.note: uneven picks the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on, of unlit B-road

explanation.surface: An unlit minor road is extremely bumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: A B-road is a British secondary road. 'uneven' looks like a description of the road surface but asks for letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra- as a prefix and ultra as a word both mean beyond normal, to an extreme degree.

clue.text: Barbarian taking crude photo? He managed to undergo ordeal, as must 1 down 24 repeatedly

definitions.text: undergo ordeal, as must 1 down 24 repeatedly

parts.note: the Goths were a barbarian people who sacked Rome
crude means rough, unrefined

indicators.note: managed, as in handled and arranged, signals rearranging the letters of photo and He

explanation.surface: A barbarian with a rough snapshot coped with hardship, like the balls in a garden game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' just joins GOTH and ROUGH; PHOTOHE rearranged under 'managed' gives the last two words. Croquet balls must pass through hoops again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffer a trying process is an idiom for undergoing an ordeal; in croquet the balls literally pass through hoops.

clue.text: Offensive article about two females going after adult material

indicators.note: about says the first pieces wrap round the others

parts.note: the Tet Offensive was a 1968 campaign in the Vietnam War

indicators.note: going after places the two Fs behind the letter for adult

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult
F is the abbreviation for female, doubled here
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A rude piece of writing concerns two women chasing a grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' is not rude here but the Tet Offensive. TET + A makes TETA, and 'about' sets AFF inside it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp woven silk fabric, a kind of dress material.

clue.text: Ruddy huge game birds used to hit 27

parts.note: ruddy and flaming are both mild British expletives
OS is the abbreviation for outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: Bloody enormous game birds were used to strike the spiny creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: In Alice in Wonderland the Queen's croquet players use flamingos as mallets to hit hedgehogs. 'Ruddy' also hints at the birds' pink colour.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's croquet match the pink wading birds serve as mallets for striking the balls.

clue.text: Disease vet identified initially in a pair of horses?

indicators.note: in says those letters sit inside the word for a pair of horses

parts.note: a span is a matched pair of draught horses

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letters of vet and identified

explanation.surface: An illness a vet spotted first in a couple of horses.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark nods to spavin being a horse disease, so the horses belong in the picture as well as the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Spavin is a swelling of a horse's hock joint, an equine ailment.

clue.text: Knocked up some satire, verbal lampooning in double quick time

indicators.note: Knocked up says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some satire was thrown together very fast, with spoken mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads a run bottom to top: EVERBALLA, inside 'satire, verbal lampooning', reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Alla breve is a musical tempo marking meaning two minim beats a bar, played twice as fast as written.

clue.text: Capital from turnover of work unit in Barry

indicators.note: turnover of says the whole assembly is read backwards
in puts the work unit inside the name

parts.note: Baz is a familiar short form of the name Barry
the erg is a unit of work or energy in physics

explanation.surface: Money comes from the business turnover of a team at Barry, in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Barry looks like the Welsh town, and 'turnover' like takings, but Barry is a man and 'turnover of' reverses BERGAZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Zagreb is the capital city of Croatia.

clue.text: Beaten in game, not having doubled spades in time

indicators.note: in says the remainder sits inside the word for time

parts.note: bird is British slang for a prison sentence, doing time

indicators.note: not having says those letters are removed from the game

parts.note: chess is a board game

indicators.note: doubled says the spades letter is written twice

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Defeated in a card game, without doubling in spades in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubled' and 'spades' suggest a bridge auction, but the game is chess, and 'in time' means inside prison time. Bird is British slang for a jail term.
explanation.definitionFit: Birched means flogged with a birch rod, so beaten as punishment.

clue.text: Maintained Welsh boy's eaten a bit of chicken

indicators.note: eaten says the chicken piece goes inside the boy's name

parts.note: Aled is a Welsh boy's name, as in the singer Aled Jones
a leg is a joint of chicken

explanation.surface: Claimed a young Welshman has eaten some chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has', so the Welsh boy has eaten the chicken piece: the leg sits inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to assert it, so a thing maintained is alleged.

clue.text: Bugs concealed by soprano under a piano

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the following letters below the a and piano letters

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
hid means concealed

explanation.surface: Insects hidden by a singer beneath a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' sets HID and S below A and P.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are small sap-sucking insects, so bugs in the strict sense.

clue.text: Olympic event not initially covered — journalist no longer working

indicators.note: not says a letter is taken away

parts.note: the discus throw is an Olympic athletics event

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of covered

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A sports event went unreported, and a reporter is out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: DISCUS without C gives DISUS, then ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disused is out of use, no longer in service.

clue.text: I moved into place to finish at 1 down

indicators.note: moved into says one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to put something is to place it
ego is Latin for I

explanation.surface: I relocated to take up a position.
explanation.walkthrough: In croquet a player pegs out by hitting the central peg to end the game; it is also slang for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: To peg out in croquet is to complete the round by striking the winning peg with the ball.

clue.text: Huge bird unhappy over new location for zoo

indicators.note: over, as in covering, says the scrambled letters close round the letter for new
unhappy, as in ill at ease, signals the letters of huge bird are put out of order

explanation.surface: An enormous bird is unhappy about its new home at the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: HUGEBIRD rearranged under 'unhappy' makes EDIBURGH, and 'over' wraps it round N. The definition sounds like a zoo enclosure but means a city with a zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh Zoo is a well-known zoo in Scotland's capital city.

clue.text: Commonplace name held by god

indicators.note: held by says the name letter goes inside the god

parts.note: Baal was a Canaanite god

explanation.surface: An everyday name kept by a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means trite and ordinary, lacking originality.

clue.text: Bottle bank's half full? That's half empty, son

indicators.note: half takes the front two letters of the four in bank
half empty says the full word loses half, leaving its back two letters

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in genealogy

explanation.surface: Is a bottle bank half full, or is it half empty, my boy?
explanation.walkthrough: The optimist-pessimist question is a joke: BA is half of 'bank's', LL is what remains of 'full' half emptied, then S. Balls, British slang, means courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for nerve or courage, and so is the vulgar slang word here.

clue.text: Liberal party having a little party with a naturally occurring drug

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: little says just the first letter of the second party is used

explanation.surface: A Liberal political party holds a small gathering with a natural medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'party' is a celebration, DO; a little of the second is its first letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: L-DOPA is an amino acid found in the body and used to treat Parkinson's disease.

clue.text: Ape tucking its tail inside vital body part

indicators.note: tucking its tail inside says the last letter moves into the middle of the word

parts.note: an orang is an orang-utan, a great ape

explanation.surface: An ape folds its tail around an important part of its body.
explanation.walkthrough: ORANG moves its final G in front of the A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Organs such as heart, liver and lungs are vital parts of the body.

clue.text: Row of bushes has more than its share of 1 down 24?

parts.note: a hedge is a row of bushes
to hog is to take more than one's share

explanation.surface: A hedgerow takes more than its fair portion.
explanation.walkthrough: In Alice in Wonderland, the Queen's croquet game uses live hedgehogs as balls, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's story the croquet balls are curled-up spiny animals, so they stand in for the game's balls.

clue.text: Fought with unruly youth about Soviets finally changing sides

indicators.note: about says the youth wraps round the rest

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth known for rowdy behaviour

indicators.note: finally changing sides says the last letter, R for right, swaps to L for left

parts.note: USSR is the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics

explanation.surface: Brawled with a rowdy youngster over the Soviets switching allegiance in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing sides' sounds political, but it means R (right) becoming L (left) in the final letter of the Soviet abbreviation, giving USSL. A Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To tussle is to scuffle or struggle, so fought in a brief physical way.

clue.text: Artificial stimulant once put in port

indicators.note: put in says the letters for once go inside the port

parts.note: Said, or Port Said, is the Egyptian port at the Suez Canal
ex means former, what once was

explanation.surface: Something artificially arousing was once landed at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' does not take Port as part of the name: Said alone is the port, and EX goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sex aid is a device used to stimulate sexual arousal.
